key_insight: HVD introduces a human-vision inspired, coarse-to-fine alignment that lets a text-video retrieval model focus on salient frames and regions, reducing background noise and improving cross-modal matching.
problem_solved: Addresses 'blind' feature interaction in CLIP-style text-video retrieval where sparse textual queries and noisy backgrounds prevent the model from identifying key visual information.
method: Coarse frame-level alignment: identify and weight video frames that are globally relevant to the text query.
Fine-grained region/patch-level alignment: apply human-vision driven saliency or attention to localize and align important visual regions with textual tokens.
Dual-level contrastive/cross-modal learning: jointly train coarse and fine alignments to produce discriminative, interpretable video representations for retrieval.
impact: Makes text-video retrieval more accurate and interpretable by focusing modeling capacity on semantically relevant visual cues; useful for practitioners building robust multimodal search and indexing systems.

paper_title: HVD: Human Vision-Driven Video Representation Learning for Text-Video Retrieval
paper_authors: Zequn Xie, Xin Liu, Boyun Zhang, Yuxiao Lin, Sihang Cai
